device_identification.name: Grating-assisted contra-directional coupler (sidewall-Bragg-grating filter)
device_identification.evidence: Central coupling region = three parallel horizontal elements: TOP comb of isolated full-height teeth (grating), MIDDLE solid straight bar (bus waveguide), BOTTOM comb of teeth (grating). Two inverse-taper 'needle' edge couplers (top-left tip points left; bottom-right tip points right). Two 180-degree U-bends (hairpins): top-right folds the top grating arm back to a return guide; bottom-left folds the bottom grating arm to the lower guide. A top-left input bend enters from the chip edge and sweeps down into the top grating.
device_identification.how_it_works: Each corrugated guide is a sidewall Bragg grating: forward-propagating light is contra-directionally coupled into the BACKWARD mode of the adjacent bus when the phase-match (Bragg) condition lambda_B = 2*n_eff*Lambda is met. The grating pair + central bus form the coupler; the reflection band is centered at lambda_B with bandwidth and peak reflectivity set by kappa*L. Inverse tapers are edge couplers (spot-size converters) for fiber/chip I/O; the hairpins route the folded arms so both ports reach the chip facet.

function_knobs.grating_period: Bragg period Lambda -> sets phase-match wavelength lambda_B (PRIMARY spectral knob).
function_knobs.grating_length: coupling / transfer length L of the top grating -> sets kappa*L (bandwidth & peak reflectivity). CHOSEN as the most-important knob for verify_knob_response.
function_knobs.corrugation_height: tooth vertical extent -> corrugation amplitude -> coupling strength kappa.
function_knobs.coupler_gap: gap between each grating and the central bus -> evanescent overlap -> kappa; also sets the band y-spacing.
function_knobs.bus_width: central bus waveguide width -> its n_eff (phase matching).
function_knobs.taper_length / tip_width: inverse-taper edge-coupler geometry -> mode-size conversion efficiency.

calibration_note: footprint=[18.24,0.70] um mapped anisotropically (scale_x=200.05, scale_y=1620 px/um; sy/sx=8.098). Device designed in isotropic visual frame (18.24 x 5.67 um) then Y-squished by 8.098 so the written GDS bbox = 18.24 x 0.70 um; the evaluator's y-stretch inverts the squish exactly.
